comments.content: Using `url.QueryEscape` for user/password is incorrect here. `url.UserPassword` already handles escaping when serializing the URL, and `QueryEscape` encodes spaces as `+` (form encoding) rather than `%20`, which will produce wrong credentials for passwords containing spaces or special characters. Pass the raw values: `u.User = url.UserPassword(config.User, config.Password)`.

`url.PathEscape` on the database name is unnecessary and can be harmful: `url.URL.String()` already escapes the path, so double-escaping will occur for names with special characters. Also, `PathEscape` escapes `/` as `%2F` which is fine, but combined with `String()`'s own escaping it produces `%252F`. Just set `Path: "/" + config.Database`.

`getDBHost` rejects any scheme other than `mongodb`, but MongoDB also supports `mongodb+srv` (used for Atlas and other SRV-based deployments). This will break existing users who pass a `mongodb+srv://` URI. Consider allowing `mongodb+srv` as well.

The error returned when the scheme is not `mongodb` is `errIncorrectURI`, but for a malformed URI like `mongodb:/...` the test expects `errParseHost`. The current logic returns `errIncorrectURI` only when scheme != "mongodb"; for `mongodb:/username:...` the scheme is `mongodb` and `Hostname()` is empty, so `errParseHost` is returned — that matches the test. However, the test case named "Empty URI" expects `errIncorrectURI`; `url.Parse("")` returns no error and scheme is `""`, so this works. No change needed, but the error naming is misleading — `errIncorrectURI` really means "unsupported scheme".

The debug log now prints `c.config.Host` instead of the actual URI. When the user supplies a `URI` (and `Host` is empty), this log will print an empty host, losing useful diagnostic info. Consider logging the resolved `host` variable returned from `generateMongoURI` instead.
